world_status: a description exists but is not accessible
sweep_summary: Both title-keyword items are false positives: Kaland 2022 (Greek/German/Portuguese macro-rhythm) and Jun 2011 (Korean/English/Japanese focus prosody) were fetched sources in full, saved, and contain no mention of Patamona; Glottolog attaches them to pbc by automatic assignment. Patamona is not in the catalog and no first-hand Patamona/Ingarikó stress statement could be read: the two likely sources are Edwards 1978 (Anthropological Linguistics 20(2), JSTOR 30027529, paywalled behind a client challenge) and Sousa Cruz 2005, Fonologia e gramática Ingarikó (VU Amsterdam; Ingarikó = Patamona per Glottolog alt names; VU portal blocked, no open copy found) — both high priority to acquire. Closest read statement is Edwards 1977 p. 36 for Akawaio/Arekuna (stress tends to the 2nd syllable in 2-3 syllable words, 3rd syllable in longer words, many exceptions); Caesar-Fox 2003's Akawaio phonology sketch is silent on stress.org, Etnolinguistica and direct fetches. new_statements.quote: There is a general tendency for main stress in Akawaio and Arekuna to fall on the second syllable in two-syllable words. In three-syllable words main stress tends to fall on the second syllable and in words of more than three syllables the third syllable tends to attract primary stress. There are, however, many exceptions to these tendencies. Different stress patterns on the same string of sounds can change their meaning e.g. (Akawaio) kugwaik - a kind of ant / kugwaik - dart (Arekuna) inna - we / inna - yes (Primary or main stress is shown by the diacritic ['] placed immediately above the stressed syllable. The unmarked syllable has weak stress).
new_statements.citation: Edwards, Walter F. 1977. An Introduction to the Akawaio and Arekuna Peoples of Guyana. Georgetown: Amerindian Languages Project, University of Guyana. Chapter V, Section II, 'Some Phonological Traits of Akawaio and Arekuna', (ii) Word Stress.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Main stress is on the second syllable of two- and three-syllable words and on the third syllable of words of four or more syllables (a left-edge count: second, second, third), but only as a tendency; many exceptions, and stress placement can distinguish otherwise identical words. NOTE: this describes Akawaio and Arekuna (Pemón), not Patamona.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; 'the unmarked syllable has weak stress'.
new_statements.exceptions: 'There are, however, many exceptions to these tendencies'; minimal pairs differing only in stress (Akawaio kugwaik 'a kind of ant' vs 'dart'; Arekuna inna 'we' vs 'yes'); vowel length separately contrastive.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level primary stress in citation forms of Akawaio and Arekuna; a non-technical introductory description ('Many details and finer distinctions will be suppressed in the interest of brevity and simplicity'). Not a statement about Patamona.
new_statements.identity_note: The only stress statement obtained (Edwards 1977, pp. 36-37) describes Akawaio (akaw1239) and Arekuna (= Pemón, pemo1248), the sister Kapóng/Pemóng varieties, and does not mention Patamona (pata1262); it must not be entered as a Patamona statement. The Kapóng cluster is a dialect continuum (Akawaio, Patamona, Ingarikó); Ethnologue/Glottolog list 'Ingarikó' as an alternative name of Patamona while Glottolog's tree makes Ingarikó a dialect of Akawaio (inga1250), so Sousa Cruz 2005 (Ingarikó) would need an explicit identity ruling before use for pata1262.

new_statements.citation: Edwards, Walter F. (1977). An Introduction to the Akawaio and Arekuna Peoples of Guyana. Georgetown: Amerindian Languages Project, University of Guyana.
new_statements.reading: CAVEAT: this describes Akawaio (the other Kapong variety) and Arekuna (Pemón), not Patamona proper; no first-hand Patamona/Ingarikó stress statement was reachable. Reading: default second-syllable stress in 2- and 3-syllable words, third syllable in longer words, i.e. left-edge counting with many lexical exceptions and some contrastive stress (minimal pairs). If used for Patamona it would be by Kapong-internal extrapolation, which should be marked as such.
